tx.t: In this talk I will explain what psychologists know about memory and how students can use it. In eighteen eighty-five, the German psychologist Hermann Ebbinghaus described the forgetting curve.
He found that people forget roughly half of new material within an hour if they do not review it. In nineteen fifty-six, George Miller suggested that short-term memory holds about seven items.
Reviewing material at increasing intervals, which is called spaced repetition, helps to move it into long-term memory. Testing yourself is more effective than simply reading your notes again.
A good night of sleep after studying helps to store what you have learned.

tx.t: Today I would like to outline what glaciers are, and why they matter for sea level. Glaciers cover about ten per cent of the world's land area.
Together, glaciers and ice sheets store about two thirds of the world's fresh water. A glacier forms when snow builds up for many years and is pressed into dense ice.
Since nineteen hundred, the global sea level has risen by about twenty centimetres. This rise is caused partly by melting ice and partly because warm water takes up more space.

tx.t: This lecture is about a successful conservation project in Fenwick Marsh. In nineteen ninety-two, only fifteen pairs of water voles were counted there.
The main reason for the decline was disturbance from walkers and dogs. So volunteers and rangers created protected zones with quiet paths.
By twenty fourteen, the number had risen to one hundred and twenty-five pairs, which shows that careful management can work.

tx.t: Today I would like to talk about the history of the Olympic Games. The ancient Games began in seven hundred and seventy-six BC at Olympia in Greece.

They were held every four years for about twelve centuries, until they were banned in the late fourth century. The modern Games were revived in eighteen ninety-six in Athens, mainly through the efforts of a Frenchman, Pierre de Coubertin.
Women first took part in the Games in nineteen hundred, in Paris. The first Winter Games were held in nineteen twenty-four at Chamonix, in France.
Today, thousands of athletes from more than two hundred countries compete in the summer Games.

tx.t: Today I would like to describe a bike-sharing scheme in the town of Fenwick. It began in twenty thirteen with two hundred and forty-one bikes, placed at stations around the centre.
Use grew quickly. Within three years the number of journeys had risen by eighty-two per cent, and on a busy day there were more than nine thousand trips.
The scheme soon met a serious problem: bikes being left in the wrong places. The council solved it with marked parking zones with a small fine for leaving a bike outside them.
Today, a ride costs one pounds thirty-five for the first half hour, and the first fifteen minutes are free for residents.

tx.t: In today's lecture we will study volcanoes and the damage they can do. There are around one thousand three hundred and fifty potentially active volcanoes in the world.
About three quarters of them lie around the Pacific Ocean, in an area called the Ring of Fire. In the year seventy-nine, the eruption of Mount Vesuvius buried the Roman town of Pompeii.

In eighteen fifteen, Mount Tambora in Indonesia erupted so violently that the following year became known as the year without a summer. The ash from large eruptions can block sunlight and cool the whole planet for a year or more.
Scientists measure small earthquakes and gas emissions to try to predict eruptions.

The students who used the method of studying at the same time each day felt less stressed before the exam. The researchers concluded that how you study may matter more than how long you study.

tx.t: Today I would like to describe a bike-sharing scheme in the town of Ashby. It began in twenty ten with six hundred and thirty-one bikes, placed at stations around the centre.
Use grew quickly. Within three years the number of journeys had risen by thirty-three per cent, and on a busy day there were more than thirteen thousand trips.
The scheme soon met a serious problem: bikes being left in the wrong places. The council solved it with marked parking zones with a small fine for leaving a bike outside them.
Today, a ride costs one pounds forty for the first half hour, and the first fifteen minutes are free for residents.
